Bulk actions work end to end. Refresh **http://maker:4001**.

**Flow 11 — bulk actions.**
1. Each bookmark now has a **checkbox** on its left. **Tick two or three.** A dark **action bar** appears at the top showing how many you've selected.
2. From that bar, try **Mark to read** — all selected move to your reading list at once. The bar also offers **Mark as read**, **Archive** (or **Restore** when you're in the Archived view), **Add tag…**, **Remove tag…**, and **Delete**.
3. **Add tag…** → type a tag (e.g. `project`) → **Apply** — it's added to every selected bookmark.
4. **Delete** → the bar asks you to confirm *"Permanently delete N bookmarks?"* with the same permanent-vs-archive wording; **Cancel** leaves them, **Delete N permanently** removes them together.

**The whole-collection safeguard you asked for:**
5. Run a **search** or pick a **view** first, tick one item, and you'll see **"Select all N shown"** — clicking it selects **only the bookmarks in that search/view**, and a line spells out *"Select all shown covers just this search/view, never your whole collection."* There's no control that silently selects everything.

Two decisions to confirm:
- **Applying an action targets exactly the ticked bookmarks** (which can include ones scrolled off or filtered out after you ticked them) — the count always reflects the true number. Is that the right rule?
- For **Remove tag…** I have you type the tag name. Would you prefer to *pick from tags actually present* on the selected bookmarks instead?
